subject: Temporary SLO carveout for traffic experiment — request and safeguards
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01 09:14 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLO carveout for A/B experiment

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from our side — we're planning a targeted A/B rollout of a new ranking tweak on Dec 3–5 to a subset of US traffic. Early internal tests look promising but we expect a short-lived increase in p95 latency for a small fraction of requests while the new model warms caches.

Two asks: can Redwood sign a temporary SLO carveout (72 hours) for this experiment that allows an elevated p95 threshold for the affected route, and can we set an automatic fallback/pinning rule so that traffic reverts to the current production variant if latency or error rate exceed agreed thresholds?

We want to avoid a full rollback — automatic fallback + version pin on degrade would be ideal. Please let us know what telemetry thresholds you need, any approval chain, and whether there are any commercial implications.

Thanks,
Sara Klein
Sr. Product Manager — ACME Data

Sofia / team — technical proposal below. Keeping it conservative and automatable.

Summary plan (can be implemented via runtime rules + rollout controller):
- Canary ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 30/90/180 minutes (manual advance unless all gates green).
- Safety gates (continuous): p95 latency, total error rate, and tail queue length.
- Autorevert triggers (immediate rollback to prior variant when ANY condition holds for window):
  - p95 latency > 350 ms for 5 consecutive minutes OR
  - error rate > 1% for 2 consecutive minutes OR
  - observed increase in 99th percentile queue time > 50% for 5 minutes.
- Pin semantics: when autorevert occurs, tie traffic to the prior pinned version for 30 minutes, during which new variant is marked as quarantined. Pin expires automatically unless ops manually unpins.
- Telemetry & alerting: create a temporary dashboard scoped to route + experiment id; send alerts to oncall and to ACME's acme-data-eng distribution.
- Human-in-loop: automatic rollback still informs oncall and product; we allow manual override to unquarantine only after post-mortem.

Runtime artifacts and IDs to apply:
- rollout_config: RB-4821
- experiment_tag: acme-dec3-ranking-v2
- fallback_policy: FP-721-autorevert

Operational notes:
- Requires ops change to enable auto-pinning for their tenant; needs a 4-hour maintenance window for the toggle to be flipped and verified.
- We will stage a dry-run traffic test on Dec 2 in our staging region to validate metrics and alert thresholds.

I'll draft the short-runbook (attached as runbook-canary-params.md) and push the runtime config once we have commercial sign-off.

— Marcus

- There is a possible premium for reserved capacity or prioritized rollback handling; I'll flag to ACME.

Sara — thanks for the quick responses. Short summary and next steps (Dec 3–5 experiment):

1) Agreement: Redwood can provision a 72-hour, time-limited SLO carveout for the named experiment (acme-dec3-ranking-v2) with the technical guardrails Marcus proposed.

2) Autorevert & pin: autorevert triggers = p95 > 350 ms for 5m OR error rate > 1% for 2m. If autorevert occurs we will pin to prior version for 30 minutes.

3) Ops prep: Marcus/ops will flip the runtime toggle and run a staging dry-run on Dec 2. ACME to provide exact route names and primary oncall contact in the signed form.

4) Paperwork & billing: Lauren attached SLA-exception-form.pdf. Please sign via DocuSign (link below). Any premium for reserved capacity will be included on the form.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ACME-SLO-EXCEPTION-2026
Runbook (preview): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AcmeRunbook

I'll be your point of contact for coordination during the window. If ACME signs by end-of-day Dec 2, we can complete the ops prep and proceed with the Dec 3 start.

Best,
